[M] To work out the rolls for the election, I will be using 2015 results, in game events, and the recent IRL council elections that happened in the UK a few days ago. To summarise council elections: SNP did very well in Scotland, UKIP did ok (but it looked like they did way better because they were running for positions they had not been in the running for before), Labour did shit in Scotland and lost a few places in England/Wales but they did take some Conservative positions, Conservatives held pretty much everything they had before, Green Party had a small bump in popularity in certain places, and a few shitty parties such as Plaid Cymru in Wales did well. Lib Dems took a couple of things but who gives a shit about the Lib Dems anyway.

----------

For those who are unaware how UK elections work, the country is split up into 650 constituencies, all of which elect an MP that belongs to a certain party. That MP then gets a seat. To win an election, a party has to get a majority of those 650 seats, failing that, there will be a coalition government under certain conditions. This has happened very few times in British history, but has happened IRL recently. We elect coalition governments when nobody has a majority , and we are at war, or there is a financial crisis/something similar. In game, I have left the EU, meaning that the conditions are right for a coalition government if nobody has a majority, which I suspect will be the case.

----------

#Rolls

Each party will be given a minimum amount of seats that they will hold in this election, based on things I have listed above. Parties will also be given a maximum amount of seats they can hold in this election (Example: There is no way the Green Party will win the election with a majority). They will then be rolled for to determine how many extra seats they get, with the most popular parties being rolled first, and the least popular being rolled last.

#Minimum Seats and Rolls For Maximum Seats

Note: Because these elections are so stupid, I will have to adjust the roll table for other parties after the Conservatives have been rolled for.

* Conservatives - Seats: 230 * Labour - Seats: 330 * SNP - Seats: 61 * Lib Dems - Seats: 17 * UKIP - Seats: 8 * Plaid Cymru - Seats: 5 * Green Party - Seats: 5 * Sinn Fein - Seats: 2 * Democratic Unionist Party - Seats: 2
